chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Fudayl and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the Prayer of Fear during skirmishing, close combat, and the clash of fighting, then every person among them prays by nodding (gesturing) wherever their face is. And when it is the continuous fighting and close engagement and the clash of battle, then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) on the night of Siffin, which is the night of Harir, did not pray with them the Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha prayers at the time of each prayer except by Takbir, Tahleel, Tasbih, Tamjid, and Du'a. So that was their prayer, and he did not order them to repeat the prayer.

And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the Prayer of Battle, and he said: 'When they meet and fight, then the prayer at that time is by Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar). And when they are standing, then the prayer is by nodding (gesturing).'
ai.seo_question: How is the Prayer of Fear (Salat al-Khawf) performed during intense battle according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the flexibility of Salat al-Khawf, distinguishing between light skirmishing where prayer is performed by nodding (I'ima') and intense close combat where Imam Ali (AS) at Siffin led prayers using only verbal glorification (Takbir, Tahlil, Tasbih) without full ritual movements. The narration emphasizes that this abbreviated prayer was considered sufficient and did not require later repetition (Qada), reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams in adapting worship to the exigencies of battle. This ruling underscores the principle of ease in hardship, allowing soldiers to maintain spiritual connection even when physical movement is impossible during direct engagement.
